# Limitations {#sec-limitations}

**The search window is too small to rank rules.** It is
`r p6_fn(p6_universe$n_val_races)` races. Cross-half rank correlations run
between `r p6_fcor(min(p6_guard_summary$spearman))` and
`r p6_fcor(max(p6_guard_summary$spearman))`, and the rule that won on both
halves reversed by
`r sprintf("%.0f", 100 * (p6_row(p6_round3_ranks$table, "win", "P4 / field size 11-12")$val_roi - p6_row(p6_round3_ranks$table, "win", "P4 / field size 11-12")$test_roi))`
points out of sample. Nothing here has identified a good rule.

**Search-set rank predicts test rank negatively on all four markets.** Round
2's positive place-market correlation did not replicate. The only difference
between the two rounds is which seven rules were in the shortlist.

**Twenty-eight rule-by-market combinations were read against one test split
with no multiplicity correction.** The intervals are marginal 90% race-level
bootstraps and are not adjusted for having looked twenty-eight times. Whatever
tops a test table is partly noise. The two rules that did top them were
carried forward unconditionally rather than selected, which is the only reason
their position means anything.

**Only the betting rule is clean.** The model was selected with knowledge of
these test races across five papers: features, objective, function class,
encoder architecture and the rung ladder were each chosen after seeing earlier
papers' test results. The split has been scored once per paper, six times on
the same races. Paper 6 fits nothing, so its betting rules are out of sample.
The model underneath them is not.

**Going and class were not really tested.** Their absence from the results is
a fact about the scope of this series (four All-Weather courses, class 2 to 5
handicaps, 2006 to 2015), not evidence that either is uninformative.

**Field size is the only race characteristic with real coverage.** The winning
band, 11 to 12 runners, is
`r p6_fpct(sum(p6_overround_val$n_races[p6_overround_val$field_size %in% 11:12]) / p6_universe$n_val_races, 1)`
of the search set, and a rule on it bets
`r p6_fn(p6_row(p6_round3_ranks$table, "win", "P4 / field size 11-12")$test_bets)`
times on test. That is not enough for its ROI to mean much either way.

**The place prices are a construction and the each-way market is not a
market.** Set out in @sec-forward.

**The forward strategy is untested.** @sec-forward reads paper 4's result
alongside a market-structure argument. Its two load-bearing assumptions, that
usable size exists at early prices and that the model beats an early traded
price, are not tested anywhere in this series and cannot be tested on this
archive.
